increment_paragraph: **TEST-STORAGE-BUDGET** (user request of 2026-10-29: the test suites within about 15 GB of CI disk, with dynamic linking for test executables; [report](../../reports/test-storage-budget/README.md)). A fresh `cargo test --workspace` peaked at 87.4 GB (583 statically linked test executables, mean 124 MB, mostly DWARF line tables and copies of the analysis crates). `scripts/test_link_config.py` now names the test-build configuration once: no incremental state, and on Linux `build.rustc-wrapper` = `scripts/rustc_test_dylib.py`, which emits every root-workspace library as a Rust dylib beside its rlib and links every test executable, binary and example dynamically against them and `libstd`, with absolute run paths (so `env_clear` children still load), withholding rustc's early metadata signal so cargo waits for each `.so`. `run_test_binaries.py` (both gates), the scoped gate's reevaluation examples and CI's Linux test steps pass it; no manifest, lockfile or cargo configuration file changes, so release builds and `measure` `rev:` sides are untouched (slice identity check skipped for that reason). Measured from empty targets: the gate's run 3.76 GB (was 87.40), 8,927 passed / 0 failed / 15 ignored with the identical test set (names per executable, ignored and failed sets compared by `compare_tests.py`), the same per-executable run time in isolation. Windows links statically and runs the full suite as `run_test_binaries.py --jobs 1 --batch-size 32` (new: build, capture, run and delete per batch, fail-closed coverage check over the whole run), measured on Linux at 6.19 GB with the same test set; not yet run on Windows. `providers/Cargo.toml` gets `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"`: the provider suite 14.97 → 5.15 GB, 133 / 0 / 1 equal, packages byte-identical with and without it. CI sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` in the Linux and Windows jobs. Policy: validation.md "Test build storage". No analyzer, contract, verdict or Lean change.

ledger.title: The Windows full-suite leg's batched runner has not run on Windows
ledger.text: TEST-STORAGE-BUDGET moved CI's msvc-clang-analysis full suite from `cargo test --workspace` to `python scripts/run_test_binaries.py --jobs 1 --batch-size 32` (static linking, batches built, run and deleted). The batched mode ran green on Linux in static mode with --jobs 8 (8,927 / 0 / 15, test set equal to the base, 6.19 GB peak), but never on Windows or with --jobs 1; the first CI run is its first Windows execution. Check that run's totals against the Linux figure and its per-batch deleted_bytes in summary.json; a dynamic Windows build would first need the DLL export counts of the large crates measured against the 65,535 limit.

ledger.title: The CI rust job's whole-sequence disk peak is estimated, not measured
ledger.text: TEST-STORAGE-BUDGET measured the root suite (3.76 GB), the provider suite (5.15 GB), Clippy (0.15 GB) and the package build's release target (0.1 GB) separately; the job keeps both workspaces' targets, so its peak is estimated at about 10.5-11 GB, including about 1.3 GB that `providers/package.py build`'s source-mode probe (a plain `cargo run` in the root workspace, without the test configuration) rebuilds statically beside the dynamic build. Measure the job's sequence once on a fresh checkout, and consider passing the test configuration to that probe.

ledger.title: Provider package executables differed between two checkouts of the same sources
ledger.text: Observed by TEST-STORAGE-BUDGET: `providers/package.py build` in a clone of 62c8e461c and in the card's worktree (same Rust sources, different checkout path and HEAD) produced different provider executables for all five packages, while the worktree with and without the card's providers/Cargo.toml change produced byte-identical ones. package.py remaps the repository path prefix, so the remaining difference (path-dependent metadata hashes of path dependencies outside the provider workspace, or a revision embedded at build time) is unidentified; if package digests are meant to be reproducible across checkouts, find it.
